ukmt-grey-2025-05.title: Subtract the double counting
ukmt-grey-2025-05.body:
If the circles did not overlap, the total area would be $5\times8=40\ \text{cm}^2$. Each of the four overlapping regions has been counted twice, so subtract each once: $40-4\times1=36\ \text{cm}^2$.

**Answer: (B) $36\ \text{cm}^2$**

ukmt-grey-2025-06.title: Use groups
ukmt-grey-2025-06.body:
If Ria has $2x$ £2 coins then she has $3x$ £1 coins (50% more). The total is $3x\times1+2x\times2=7x=35$, so $x=5$ and she has $2x=10$ £2 coins.

**Answer: (B) 10**

ukmt-grey-2025-06.title: Check the answer
ukmt-grey-2025-06.body:
Try 10 two-pound coins: £20, and 15 one-pound coins: £15. The total is £35 and $15=1.5\times10$. ✓

**Answer: (B) 10**

ukmt-grey-2025-09.title: Go round the ring
ukmt-grey-2025-09.body:
Name the empty circles going round: the top circle $p$, then (clockwise) the circle next to 2 is $s$, the grey bottom circle is $r$, and the circle next to 1 is $q$.

The top circle is between the circles with 1 and 2, so $p=1+2=3$. The circle with 1 is between $p$ and $q$, so $1=3+q$ and $q=-2$. The circle with 2 is between $p$ and $s$, so $2=3+s$ and $s=-1$. The grey circle is between $q$ and $s$, so it holds $-2+(-1)=-3$.

**Answer: (D) $-3$**

ukmt-grey-2025-11.title: The denominator must divide 77
ukmt-grey-2025-11.body:
The eight primes below 20 are $2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19$, with sum $77$. All eight boxes get a different prime, so if the denominator is $Y$ the numerator is $77-Y$ and $X=\dfrac{77-Y}{Y}=\dfrac{77}{Y}-1$.

For $X$ to be an integer, $Y$ must divide $77=7\times11$, so $Y=7$ or $Y=11$. The larger value of $X$ comes from the smaller $Y$: $X=\dfrac{77}{7}-1=10$.

**Answer: (C) 10**

ukmt-grey-2025-12.title: Work backwards from d
ukmt-grey-2025-12.body:
Since the numbers are integers, $d<100$ gives $d\le99$. Then $c<4d\le396$, so $c\le395$. Then $b<3c\le1185$, so $b\le1184$. Finally $a<2b\le2368$, so $a\le2367$, and this value is achieved by $d=99,\ c=395,\ b=1184,\ a=2367$.

**Answer: (C) 2367**

ukmt-grey-2025-14.title: Compare with the current means
ukmt-grey-2025-14.body:
Bowl X has total $1+2+6+7+10+11+12=49$, so its mean is $49\div7=7$. Bowl Y has total $29$ and mean $29\div5=5.8$.

Removing a ball raises the mean of X only if the ball is below 7, and adding a ball raises the mean of Y only if the ball is above 5.8. The only ball in X that is below 7 and above 5.8 is 6.

**Answer: (E) 6**

ukmt-grey-2025-20.title: Compare the times for the second half
ukmt-grey-2025-20.body:
The second half normally takes 2 hours $=120$ minutes. After a 40-minute stop, the second half must be done in $120-40=80$ minutes.

Speed is inversely proportional to time for the same distance, so the new speed is $\dfrac{120}{80}=1.5$ times the old speed, an increase of 50%.

**Answer: (C) 50**

ukmt-grey-2025-20.title: Use numbers
ukmt-grey-2025-20.body:
Say the whole trip is 240 km, so the speed is 60 km/h. The second half is 120 km and must take $1\tfrac{1}{3}$ hours, needing $120\div\tfrac43=90$ km/h. That is 30 km/h more than 60, i.e. 50% more.

**Answer: (C) 50**

ukmt-grey-2025-24.title: Open box D
ukmt-grey-2025-24.body:
If D holds gold, she has found it. If D holds red, then A (gold or red) holds gold. If D holds pink, then B (pink or black) holds black, so C (black or gold) holds gold. If D holds white, then E (pink or white) holds pink, so B holds black, and again C holds gold. So opening D always settles it.

Other boxes can fail. For example, if Lilly opens A and sees red, the boxes B, C, D, E could hold (pink, black, gold, white), (black, gold, pink, white) or (black, gold, white, pink); in the first D holds gold and in the others C does, so she cannot tell. (Boxes B, C and E can be shown not to work in a similar way.)

**Answer: (D)**

ukmt-grey-2025-25.title: Locate the four birds
ukmt-grey-2025-25.body:
Call the wires W, X, Y, Z from the top. Neither Ha nor Long can be on W (some bird is above each). Neither Nha nor Trang can be on Z. Long has more birds above than Ha, so Long is on a lower wire than Ha. Nha has 5 below and Trang has 2 below, so Nha is on a higher wire than Trang.

Suppose Nha were on W. Every bird on W is above Ha (Ha is not on W), so W holds at most 10 birds. The birds not below Nha are exactly those on W, so the total would be at most $10+5=15$. But Long has 25 birds above, so there are at least 26 birds. Contradiction. So Nha is on X and Trang on Y.

Long is on Y or Z. If Long were on Y with Trang, Trang would have 25 birds above and 2 below, but 25 is not a multiple of 2. So Long is on Z, which holds only the 2 birds below Trang, including Long.

The total is the 25 above Long plus the 2 on Z (Long and one other): $25+2=27$.

**Answer: (A) 27**
